newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPALS -- softer, awaiting NYC water debt.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPALS -- softer, awaiting NYC water debt.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in early trade Tuesday were flat to down about an 1/8 point as the market looked ahead to some key sales, including New York City Water bonds and Georgia general obligations.

The early read on the market's tone pointed to a fairly quiet day as traders said fixed-income markets appeared to be settling into a new, lower range after getting stung on Friday by some surprisingly robust economic data on payrolls and manufacturing.
"It'll be tentative, I would anticipate a relatively quiet day, not much in big swings, there's a little bit of economic news," one trader said.

Another trader said institutions still appeared reluctant to sell in any volume because they seemed to be hoping that prices would recover, though he was doubtful. "My personal feeling is that we're just going to settle down here for awhile.
He also looked for fairly muted activity, explaining new bonds sold by municipal issuers as well as the Treasury's auctions looked likely to dominate trading.

Georgia at 1100 EDT was slated to offer $240 million of bonds in a competitive sale, while underwriters for the New York City Water Finance Authority planned to price for institutions approximately $365 million of revenue bonds.

However, individual investors only placed orders for about $12 million of bonds during a presale retail order period, a disappointing result that reflected the uncertainity caused by the market's recent volatility.
The retail order scale was revamped Monday with yields that were 20 basis points higher, with a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2018, the longest maturity that was offered to retail.

The Treasury kicks off a three-part, $38 billion refunding at 1300 EDT by selling $16 billion of three-year notes. That sale is followed by an auction of $12 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday, and $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.

While it is not uncommon for prices to edge lower as dealers clean out their shelves to make room for the new issues, there has been speculation that part of Friday's selling, which saw a bit of follow through on Monday, already might have taken care of this.
In Chicago debt futures, the September municipal contracts eased one tick to 114-20/32. The September Treasury bond contracts shed two ticks to 120-12/32. The MOB spread stood at at 184 ticks .
The main guage of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List stood at $1.4 billion.
Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were offered at 5.35 percent, NET.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority bonds of 2024, which pay a 5.0 percent coupon, were bid at 5.45 percent, NET, up one basis point.
